target.name: Ran mediated mitosis
target.description: The Ran GTPase gradient that governs nuclear transport in interphase is reused in mitosis to tell a cell where chromosomes are, and this pathway covers that use. Because the nuclear envelope has broken down, RanGTP generated on chromatin marks the chromosomal neighbourhood, releasing importin-bound spindle assembly factors such as TPX2 from KPNA2 so that microtubule nucleation and branching occur near chromosomes rather than at random; RANBP1 helps keep the gradient steep.

target.name: Assembly and cell surface presentation of NMDA receptors
target.description: NMDA receptors are the glutamate-gated, calcium-permeable channels that make excitatory synapses plastic, and this pathway covers how they are built and delivered to the neuronal surface. target.name: Defective SLC5A7 in the neurotransmitter release cycle causes distal hereditary motor neuronopathy 7A (HMN7A)
target.description: Cholinergic neurons cannot make their own choline, so they must retrieve it from the synaptic cleft after acetylcholine is hydrolysed, and the high-affinity, sodium- and chloride-dependent choline transporter encoded by SLC5A7 performs that retrieval at the presynaptic terminal. Because choline uptake is the rate-limiting step in acetylcholine synthesis, this transport step sets how much transmitter can be reloaded into vesicles during sustained firing, making it part of the neurotransmitter release and recycling cycle rather than a peripheral metabolic detail.

target.description: Retrograde traffic from early endosomes back to the Golgi recovers receptors, enzymes and membrane that would otherwise be degraded in lysosomes, sustaining repeated rounds of secretion and sorting. Mannose-6-phosphate receptors, TGN SNAREs and cargo adaptors are returned by this route, and it is also the path hijacked by Shiga and cholera toxins to reach the ER.
